newsitem.title: USA: Pentagon sets tighter watch for merger threats.
newsitem.headline: Pentagon sets tighter watch for merger threats.

text.p: The Pentagon said Tuesday it will mount a tighter watch for potential damage from U.S. defense industry mergers on the future cost, quality and availability of military weapons.

Defense Undersecretary Paul Kaminski said he was taking steps recommended in a new study to avoid possible harm to smaller firms from such mega-mergers as Boeing Co.'s planned $14 billion acquisition of McDonnell Douglas Corp.

Pentagon officials worry that mergers are creating industry giants that can build arms without buying parts and services from other companies, battering competition in the nation's military-industrial base.

Kaminski released a study by the Defense Science Board Task Force on Vertical Integration and Supplier Decisions. It recommended, among other steps, better training of Pentagon anti-trust watchers and careful monitoring of key products and technology to recognize future problems from mergers.
"I endorse the report and I have directed that the recommendations be implemented fully and immediately," Kaminski told reporters.
Kaminski said the report did not have any evidence that mergers were yet creating systemic problems at the Defense Department.
But the report concluded that the Pentagon "is not well postured in its ongoing acquisition management process to recognize or address problems emerging as a result of vertical integration."

Federal regulators have not yet given any formal go-ahead to the planned merger of Boeing and McDonnell, a move which would create a firm with some 200,000 employes and annual sales of nearly $50 billion.
